common_name: Aureum Golden Wood Millet (Bowles' Golden Grass)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich, slightly acidic to neutral soil in partial to full shade; this golden-leaved selection holds its color best where it gets some morning light but is shielded from hot afternoon sun.

directions: Unlike the green-leaved wild species, this selection holds true golden-yellow foliage from spring through the first hot stretches of summer, when color often softens toward chartreuse before cooling autumn weather restores the brighter gold. Loose, open flower panicles dangle on wiry stems just above the foliage in late spring, carrying tiny gold-tinted seeds that shine when backlit in dappled shade. Because seedlings from 'Aureum' frequently come up gold as well, established plantings tend to self-sow into a naturalized colony rather than staying as a single clump, so gardeners who want a tidy specimen should deadhead before seed drop. Division of named clumps in spring is the surest way to propagate plants that match the parent exactly.
